findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine was observed to be sanitizing at 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The inspector primed the sanitizer and the dish machine was observed to sanitize at 100ppm of Chlorine. This was discussed with the PIC. The dish machine should be being tested daily using the Chlorine test strips that are available in the facility. A spot check will be conducted to ensure that the dish machine is sanitizing at a label-recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket on the cook-line was observed to be at 50ppm of Quaternary ammonium. The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade by the PIC and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that the sanitizer dispenser knob is being fully turned when filling up a sanitizer bucket. These buckets should be changed at least every two to four hours (more if they are heavily used) and should be frequently tested to ensure that they are at a label-recommended concentration. Staff should be trained on how to properly make a sanitizer bucket, how to test it, and how often to change them.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The facility uses white containers that are placed in the freezer and then are used to cold hold along the cook-line. Cheese in one of these containers was probed to be at 57F and 49F. Onions that are cooked and cooled were probed to be at 66F in another one of these containers. These containers should be changed out more or another method of cold holding will be needed. CORRECTED- The white containers were switched with new ones from the freezer and the cheese and onions had only been in the previous containers for a short period of time. A spot check will be conducted to ensure that TCS food items are being properly cold held.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The paper towel dispenser at the hand sinks next to the three part sink would not produce paper towels during this inspection. The PICs were told and replaced the paper towels to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

The sanitizer dispenser is not consistently producing sanitizer of correct concentration. The PICs are currently making a solution manually using a CL based sanitizer. The Quat based dispenser needs repairs and/or adjustment from the company as basic troubleshooting was not sufficient to remedy the situation. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure repairs are made.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The floor under and behind the soda syrups in the dry storage area are in need of cleaning; 2) dust has accumulated on the tubes of the walk in cooler’s fan unit; 3) the floor around and behind the ice machine is in need of cleaning. These locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean thoroughly and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that facilities are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Mops are observed stored with the heads pooled up in the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mops so that the heads could hang dry. Education was conducted. Ensure regardless of equipment the bristles or the heads are stored so that they are able to hang and drip dry efficiently.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Inspector observes the can opener to be soiled with accumulated food debris. The can opener was put through dish during the inspection. The violation is considered corrected at this time. Form a habit of cleaning the can opener after morning prep activities. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Tomatoes held in the main make table have an internal temperature of  53F.  The tomatoes and garlic aioli sauce were voluntarily discarded and replaced with fresh items. The bottom of the make table has sauces holding at 40F and jalapeños holding at 39F. The top was open for lunch and there was a pan left out of the top left corner. Take care to use equipment properly so that it maintains foods at 41F or below.  

Grilled onion in the ice crock has a probe temperature of 45F. There is a large gap between the mushrooms and grilled onions. When using this ice container gaps cannot be left. The grilled onion was discarded and new grilled onion from the walk in was placed in the ice container with ice to fill the gap. 


A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: Inspector observes the drop guard on the ice machine to have a crack in it. Repair or replace the drop guard on the ice machine. 

(A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Inspector observes the following non food contact surfaces soiled:
1 Gaskets on make tables to be soiled.
2 Make table condensers (cleaned on site)
3 Top lid of the drive up side make table
4 Fan on the make line blowing along the floor. 
5 Fan covers on the fans in the walk in cooler.
Clean these items and maintain them free of accumulated soil and dust. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Mold accumulation on the soda nozzles of the soda fountain at the drive through is significant. This causes contamination to the food running through it. The machine was shut down. All of the nozzles were removed and properly washed rinsed and sanitized before being put back on the machine, properly protected with gloved hands so that they are maintained free of contamination and do not contaminate the food. The violation was corrected on site. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the soda nozzles at the drive up soda fountain are heavily soiled with mold. These items shall be properly cleaned and sanitized at least once every 24 hours. The soda fountain was closed, nozzles removed and properly washed rinsed and sanitized. Nozzles were placed onto the machine with clean, gloved hands. Treat the soda nozzles just like a fork, knife or spoon. The violation is considered corrected on site. Maintain the soda fountain nozzles clean and sanitized. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
